# `generator-shortcuts` answer

The strongest plausible shortcut that fits the canonical demonstrations is
**`canonical_colors_only`**:

> Treat a top-panel cell as occupied only when its value is 2, treat the aligned
> bottom-panel cell as occupied only when its value is 1, and output 3 when
> either test is true.

This fits all five labeled canonical pairs because their top and bottom role
colors are always 2 and 1. It is still a shortcut: the intended rule uses
nonzero occupancy at fixed panel positions, independent of the role colors.

## Exact disagreement input

Generator recipe: seed `991`, sample index `7`, overrides
`grid_w=5`, `top_color=9`, `bot_color=8`, `sep_color=4`.

```text
9 0 0 0 9
9 0 9 9 9
0 0 0 9 9
0 0 0 9 9
4 4 4 4 4
8 8 8 8 0
0 8 0 8 8
8 0 0 8 8
0 0 0 0 0
```

The intended output is:

```text
3 3 3 3 3
3 3 3 3 3
3 0 0 3 3
0 0 0 3 3
```

The shortcut predicts a 4×5 all-zero grid, so it disagrees at 15 cells.

## How it was checked

I executed the exact canonical Racket program through `RacketBridge`; its output
matched the independent Python `rule_mirror`. I then executed the declared
shortcut on the same input and compared every cell. The complete recipe, exact
input and outputs, disagreement coordinates, generator hash, rule hash, and
canonical program hash are retained in:

`repo/generators/7d8fc2325e02/counterexamples/canonical-colors-only-shortcut.json`

The large lesson census independently confirms that the shortcut fits 5/5
canonical pairs and is refuted in every one of 300 generated production lessons.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

Yes. The selected production generator emitted the exact case above through its
public exact overrides, and its ordinary unpinned schedule also emits
noncanonical role palettes. The new `palette_generalization` semantic witness
checks this property directly. The OR/XOR parametric prototype uses the same
selected input grammar, so its episodes also include noncanonical palettes when
chosen by the sampler; however, palette generalization is part of the canonical
generator repair, not a claim that the proposed variant is production-approved.
